newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate leader favors lower interest rates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate leader favors lower interest rates.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said on Sunday he believed interest rates should be lower and that last week's market reaction to Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's comments were "a reaction to Greenspan's strength."

In an interview on Fox News Sunday, Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said the U.S. economy had experienced "a long period of stability and low interest rates," but he said he believed the Federal Reserve Board had too much power and "I think interest rates should be lower."
Greenspan's comments last week about the markets' "exuberant irrationality" rattled stock markets worldwide for a day.
Lott said, "I've always been a little nervous about the Fed ... they focus too much on one side of the equation." He added, "I don't want to bash them ... but I think interest rates should be lower."

Lott also said he favored a cut in the capital gains tax, complaining that despite low interest rates the U.S. economy growth had been "anemic." He said he planned to begin hearings on tax reform when the new Congress convenes in January.

A reduction in the capital gains tax rate would not be "just for the rich," he said, but would be aimed at taxpayers such as a Mississippi farmer with 60 acres of timber to sell who hesitates because he has to pay the capital gains tax on his profits.
"I can absolutely predict with certainty that we're going to try very hard to get some relief in that area," he said. It's something we want to do for the economy."
